What it is

A CTC model built on a Whisper-tiny encoder. It keeps the acoustic half, drops the decoder, and adds two transformer blocks and a linear CTC head over one shared Italian and English vocabulary.

At a glance

  • Whisper-tiny encoder, two extra transformer blocks, one linear CTC head.
  • 11,575,169 parameters in an 11.9 MB int8 graph; 19.7 MB for the whole package.
  • 80-bin log-mel at 16 kHz, 30 seconds per pass, no streaming.
  • Silero VAD in the loop: silence and steady noise produce no words.
  • About 47× real time on four threads, 25× on one, on an Apple M5.
  • Apache-2.0. Initial encoder weights from openai/whisper-tiny (MIT).

Moth 0.8.1 Italian speech, English terms, one small package

Moth is a CTC speech-to-text model for the way Italians actually talk: Italian sentences with English words and phrases inside them. It is built on a Whisper-tiny encoder, ships as a 19.7 MB package, and transcribes in the browser through ONNX Runtime Web.

The package contains the whole model runtime: an 11.9 MB int8 ONNX graph, a 5.4 MB trigram language model, a 2.3 MB Silero VAD, the vocabulary and the mel filterbank. No PyTorch, no Python, no server. The browser path is ONNX Runtime Web over WASM, and the audio never leaves the tab.

It is record-then-transcribe, not streaming. It writes lowercase text without punctuation and spells numbers out. Pure English is not the use case; the model is for Italian speech with English terms embedded in it.

The numbers

All figures are normalized WER and ETA on the published int8 model, decoded with beam 12, top-k 10, LM weight 0.55 and token bonus 2.7. Lower WER is better; ETA is the share of annotated English-origin words reproduced exactly.

Read the split, not just the total

  • 400 of the 600 mixed-test clips come from voices heard in training.
  • S3, the only held-out voice, is the honest speaker number: 24.96 WER.
  • FLEURS-EN is a check, not a use case: 49.81 WER on pure English.
  • The test sets are reused read speech, not a fresh natural mixed-dev.

Where it still fails

  • Pure English is weak: 49.81 WER on FLEURS-EN. This is a code-switching model, not a bilingual one.
  • No punctuation, no casing, no formatting. Numbers are spelled out in Italian.
  • Speaker coverage is three people. S1 and S2 are training voices; S3 is the only held-out voice, and it shares a recording setup with S1.
  • Music can produce words. The VAD stops silence and steady noise, not music.

What the output is not

  • It does not stream: one clip at a time, up to 30 seconds per pass.
  • It does not translate, summarise or punctuate.
  • It does not return probabilities; it returns text.
  • It does not try to be a general multilingual model.

Noise

The 0.7.0 recipe heard half of its Italian read speech through noise. That is where the noise robustness came from. 0.8.1 keeps the 0.8.0 acoustic graph and changes only the language model.

What the curve says

  • On the training noise pool, 15 dB is 27.67 WER and 10 dB is 33.79.
  • The mean from 5 to 30 dB is 29.47 WER for 0.8.1.
  • Every condition is a statistical tie with 0.8.0: the LM changed, not the acoustics.
  • One room, one take, steady ambience. Not a promise about every café or car.

What the 0.7.0 change bought

On the controlled fp32 curve, 0.7.0 gained 6.3 WER points at 15 dB and 11.5 at 10 dB over 0.6.0; clean performance was a statistical tie. On a room recorded after training the gain was larger — 11.2 points at 15 dB and 18.3 at 10 dB — because the room is harsher and the baseline falls further.

What it does not cover: one room, one take, steady ambience, a synthetic signal-to-noise ratio. The 0.8.1 curve is the same-pool measurement, not the unseen-room one.

The English words

The headline WER hides the part the model is for: the English terms inside Italian. 0.8.1 rebuilt the language model around them, without touching the acoustic graph.

What changed in 0.8.1

  • The trigram LM was rebuilt from a frozen training-side corpus, keeping every bigram and repeating term-containing sentences three times.
  • Rare aligned ETA: 28.4% → 46.9% (23/81 → 38/81).
  • Rare presence: 11/47 → 24/47.
  • T-600: 24.71 → 24.08 WER, 54.17 → 55.23 ETA.
  • Natural-term presence: 432/817, two above the pre-registered gate of 431.

What the gain costs

The LM prior helps the rare terms, but natural-term presence falls from 436/817 to 432/817: the gain is partly bought with common-term robustness. The 16-term gold check stays 19/27. The acoustic weights did not change, so this is a decode-side trade, not a new model.

Rare WER improves from 35.9% to 28.2%. The pre-registered primary gate was 30% rare aligned ETA; 0.8.1 reaches 46.9%.

How it works

No neural decoder, no language token, no generation loop. The encoder sees the audio, the CTC head emits one distribution per frame, and the decoder turns that into words.

Listen at 50 frames a second.

The front-end is Whisper's: 80-bin log-mel at 16 kHz, a 25 ms window and a 10 ms hop. Two convolutions take the sequence to 50 frames per second.

Encode, then score every frame.

Four pretrained Whisper-tiny blocks and two extra transformer blocks share one 384-wide stream. A linear head projects each frame to 1,025 CTC tokens: blank plus a 1,024-piece Italian and English BPE.

Search the words, not the text.

Prefix beam search with beam 12, top-k 10, a trigram LM at weight 0.55 and a per-token bonus of 2.7. The bonus is not optional: without it the beam under-emits and deletes words.

Front-end: 80-bin log-mel at 100 frames a second. Full model card 

import soundfile as sf
from stt.onnx_runner import ReleaseMoth

runtime = ReleaseMoth("release")
audio, sample_rate = sf.read("speech.wav", dtype="float32")
text, seconds = runtime.transcribe(audio, sample_rate=sample_rate)

What comes back

A lowercase, unpunctuated transcript and the wall-clock seconds. The input is mono 16 kHz PCM in [-1, 1]; there is no implicit resampling. The package validates its own hashes and size at load.

Try it

The live demo loads the same package through ONNX Runtime Web in the tab. Model, LM and VAD download once; the recording stays local. Nothing is sent to a server.
